title: Regional Organizations — SAARC, ASEAN, EU, AU, BIMSTEC and More
shortDescription: Membership, headquarters, and founding years for the major regional blocs — the section exams mine hardest for one-line facts.
genZNote: Same question format every time: who's in it, since when, headquartered where — just with a new acronym.

sections.heading: SAARC — South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation
bullets: Established: 8 December 1985, in Dhaka.
Headquarters (Secretariat): Kathmandu, Nepal.
8 members: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives, Afghanistan (joined 2007).
Objective: accelerate economic and social development through regional cooperation in South Asia.
SAARC summits have been irregular in recent years due to India-Pakistan tensions; India has since emphasised BIMSTEC as an alternative regional platform.

sections.heading: ASEAN — Association of Southeast Asian Nations
bullets: Established: 8 August 1967, by the Bangkok Declaration — founding members: Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand.
Headquarters (Secretariat): Jakarta, Indonesia.
10 members today (expanded to include Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Cambodia).
India holds an ASEAN 'Dialogue Partner' status (since 1992, elevated to full Dialogue Partner in 1996) and a 'Strategic Partnership' — India is NOT a full ASEAN member.
India–ASEAN cooperation is formalised through India's 'Act East Policy'.

sections.heading: European Union (EU)
bullets: Evolved from the European Coal and Steel Community (1951) and European Economic Community (1957); formally established as the 'European Union' by the Maastricht Treaty, which took effect 1 November 1993.
Headquarters: Brussels, Belgium (main EU institutions); other key institutions are in Luxembourg and Strasbourg.
27 member states (post-Brexit — the UK left the EU in January 2020).
A genuine supranational union: members share a common market, and most (not all) share a common currency, the euro, used by the 'Eurozone' subset of members.
Not all EU members use the euro, and not all European countries are EU members — these are three separate/overlapping groups (EU, Eurozone, 'Europe' as a continent).

sections.heading: African Union (AU)
bullets: Established: 2002, replacing the earlier Organisation of African Unity (OAU, founded 1963).
Headquarters: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
55 member states — essentially all of Africa.
The African Union was admitted as a permanent member of the G20 in 2023, alongside the European Union — both are regional-bloc members of G20, not country members.

sections.heading: BIMSTEC — Bay of Bengal Initiative
bullets: Established: 1997 (originally BIST-EC with 4 members; renamed BIMSTEC after Myanmar joined).
Headquarters (Secretariat): Dhaka, Bangladesh.
7 members: India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand.
Notably bridges South Asia and Southeast Asia — and, unlike SAARC, excludes Pakistan, which is one reason India has increasingly prioritised BIMSTEC.

sections.heading: SCO — Shanghai Cooperation Organisation
bullets: Established: 2001 (evolved from the 'Shanghai Five' grouping formed in 1996).
Headquarters (Secretariat): Beijing, China.
Founding members: China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan.
India and Pakistan became full members in 2017 — both joined together in the same expansion round.
Focus: regional security cooperation (originally counter-terrorism/border issues), later broadened to economic cooperation.

sections.heading: Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC)
bullets: Established: 1981.
Headquarters: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
6 members: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman.

Focus: economic, security, and social cooperation among Gulf Arab monarchies; India has a strategic partnership with the GCC given the large Indian expatriate population and energy trade ties in the region.

rows: Military-political alliance; collective defence under Article 5 of the founding treaty.
Political and economic cooperation among Pacific Island states.

sections.heading: Membership vs Observer/Dialogue Status — The Real Exam Trap
sections.body: Exams routinely test whether India is a FULL member, DIALOGUE PARTNER, OBSERVER, or has no formal status at all with a given regional body — these are not interchangeable categories.

rows: Dialogue Partner + Strategic Partner (NOT a full member)
No membership category applies (not a regional member, but has a Strategic Partnership)
No membership category applies (Strategic Partnership only)
No membership category applies (not an African state)

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Regional organizations limit membership to states of one geographic region — from SAARC (South Asia, 1985) and ASEAN (Southeast Asia, 1967) to the EU (Europe) and AU (Africa, 2002) — each with its own founding year, HQ, and membership rules.
keyFacts: SAARC: 1985, HQ Kathmandu, 8 members including Afghanistan (2007).
ASEAN: 1967, HQ Jakarta, 10 members — India is a Dialogue Partner, NOT a full member.
EU: Maastricht Treaty in force Nov 1993, HQ Brussels, 27 members post-Brexit; Eurozone ≠ EU membership.
AU: 2002 (replaced OAU, 1963), HQ Addis Ababa; AU became a permanent G20 member in 2023.
BIMSTEC: 1997, HQ Dhaka, 7 members, excludes Pakistan.
SCO: 2001, HQ Beijing; India & Pakistan both joined as full members in 2017.
commonConfusion: India is a Dialogue Partner of ASEAN, not a full member — a very common exam trap.
Being 'in Europe' geographically is not the same as being an EU member, and being an EU member is not the same as using the euro (Eurozone).

highYieldFacts: SAARC (1985, Kathmandu) has 8 members; BIMSTEC (1997, Dhaka) has 7 and excludes Pakistan.
India and Pakistan both became full SCO members in 2017, in the same expansion.
African Union became a permanent G20 member in 2023, alongside the European Union.
commonTraps: Do not upgrade India's ASEAN 'Dialogue Partner' status to full membership — it is explicitly NOT a member.
Do not confuse GCC membership (6 Gulf monarchies) with the broader Arab League (22 members) — GCC is a subset-flavoured but organizationally separate body.
mustRemember: SAARC HQ: Kathmandu. ASEAN HQ: Jakarta. AU HQ: Addis Ababa. SCO HQ: Beijing. BIMSTEC HQ: Dhaka. GCC HQ: Riyadh.
NATO's collective-defence clause is Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty (1949).

confusedTerms.distinction: SAARC (1985) covers South Asia including Pakistan and Afghanistan; BIMSTEC (1997) bridges South and Southeast Asia and excludes Pakistan — India has increasingly prioritised BIMSTEC.

possibleQuestions: What is India's membership status with ASEAN?
In which year did India and Pakistan become full members of the SCO?
